claims.text: A CALPHAD–first-principles–machine-learned-potential workflow can accurately predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for refractory high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys contain at least five principal metallic elements in approximately equimolar proportions.
Refractory high-entropy alloys are primarily composed of refractory elements and commonly form BCC solid solutions with very high melting points.
Minor Al, Ti, or Si additions can be used to tune phase stability in the proposed refractory alloy system.
CALPHAD can rapidly screen HEA composition spaces and identify candidate phase-stability regions.
First-principles KKR-CPA or DFT data can be used to develop or validate interatomic potentials for multicomponent HEAs.
Molecular-dynamics heating and cooling simulations with the trained potential can calculate melting points, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for RHEAs.
Experimental characterization in the stated regime is difficult because RHEAs have extreme melting points and high-temperature reactivity.
Size mismatch among multiple principal elements causes severe local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and changes vibrational entropy, thereby affecting melting behavior and heat capacity.
Classical force fields struggle in HEAs because suitable transferable force fields are unavailable across their broad compositional space.
Full first-principles molecular dynamics is computationally prohibitive for screening vast multicomponent composition spaces.
Restricting the search with CALPHAD reduces the combinatorial space that must be evaluated by more expensive atomistic methods.
Machine-learned potentials can capture the complex local environments and anharmonic vibrational effects needed for accurate melting predictions at much lower cost than first-principles MD.
The proposed framework will predict melting temperatures of NbMoTaW, NbMoTaWV, and related known RHEAs with less than 5% error.
The framework will correctly predict melting-point depression or elevation caused by minor V or Ti additions.
Entropy of fusion can be estimated from the simulated latent heat and melting temperature.
CALPHAD predictions for complex HEAs depend strongly on database reliability and can disagree with experiments when the database is incomplete.
The method is valid only for single-phase BCC or FCC solid solutions and may fail for phase-separated, intermetallic, or amorphous systems.
A trained potential may not transfer reliably to compositions outside its training set when local coordination environments change substantially.

contradictions.description: The initial state requires at least five elements, but NbMoTaW, repeatedly offered as a representative test system, contains only four named elements.

The predicted accuracy is less than 5% melting-temperature error, whereas falsification requires error greater than 10%. Results between 5% and 10% would violate the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
